statement: Unemployment insurance premiums ride payroll on two legs: the insured person's premium, which the employer withholds, and the employer's own premium, both transferred to the Tax and Customs Board with the corresponding return by the 10th day of the month following payment (Unemployment Insurance Act § 42(1)). The Act fixes the bands at 0.5 to 2.8% for insured persons and 0.25 to 1.4% for employers (§ 41(1), (2)), and the Government's current regulation sets the rates at 1.6% and 0.8% for 2026 through 2029.
caveat: Rates are set four years at a time by Government regulation under § 41(4) and can be amended for future calendar years; regulation no 78 of 2025-09-25 replaced the 2025-2028 regulation and kept the rates unchanged. The withholding obligation for an insured person ends at pensionable age (§ 42(1) clause 1).
